about.title: Fairfax Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Fairfax's compact downtown along Broadway and Center Boulevard draws foot traffic to shops, cafes, and trailheads, and uneven pavement, wet floors, or poorly lit stairwells can turn a routine errand into a serious injury. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and failed to fix it or post a warning. That's why documenting the scene matters so much — photos of the spill, broken step, or missing handrail, along with the names of any witnesses, can make the difference in a claim. Surveillance footage from a Marin County business or apartment complex is often overwritten within days or weeks, so early action counts. If you were hurt in a fall anywhere in Fairfax, an independent attorney in our network can review what happened and explain your options, with no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Fairfax Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't correct it in time. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Before It's Gone
items.desc: Surveillance video from Fairfax shops or apartment buildings is frequently deleted on a short cycle, and hazards like spills get cleaned up fast. Acting quickly to request and preserve footage and photos protects your claim.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced by any share of fault assigned to you, but it isn't automatically barred. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that accounts for this rule.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Fairfax?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your fall happened on public property, such as a Marin County sidewalk or building, a much shorter claims deadline can apply, so it's worth having a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I partly caused my own fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible, though the amount may be reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how facts like lighting, warning signs, or your own footwear might factor in.

items.question: I fell at a business near Sir Francis Drake Boulevard — what should I do first?
items.answer: Try to photograph the hazard, note the time and location, and ask an employee to document the incident if possible. Preserving evidence quickly matters because many Fairfax businesses only retain surveillance footage for a short window before it's automatically deleted.
